name: Six-Slot External-License Extension Schemas and Their Comparison Maps
description: Packages six-slot LCEL instances with base, license and reimport supports. Godel, benchmark and DP instances are pairwise stagewise equivalent with universal quasi-functors.

program.name: Certificates and Confession
program.summary: A construction method adds comparison data and verifies the original relation; a confession method transforms the problem, omits a coordinate and transports the result through a soundness theorem. The confession routes for the kernel share the canonical dependency-pair rank, the typed external-license schemas are related by quasi-functors with one irreversible license stage, and licensed transactions compose with ledgers while no rule recovers the composite semantic profile from the factor capabilities alone.

oneLine: Godel, benchmark-transport and DP-emitter six-slot instances compare by stagewise equivalence with universal quasi-functors when explicit comparison, admissibility and bridge witnesses are supplied.
summary: Six-slot LCEL instances package base, boundary, external license, licensed extension, reimport and annotation slots with proposition-level witness slots. The central question is when two such instances compare by stagewise equivalence and universal quasi-functors with transported reversibility and factorization packages. Canonical Godel, benchmark-transport and DP-emitter instances each realize the schema with proof-carrying supports and admit pairwise comparison witnesses. Given an unrestricted mathematical witness or classification data with admissibility plus bridge data and canonical equalities, a universal quasi-functor exists between internally built admissible instances, and the Godel-DP and benchmark-DP pairs close this form. Original boundary plus conservativity clauses force boundary-reimport disjointness, while an annotated repair with licensed return permits Godel-shaped overlap and is strictly weaker. Realization alone yields a subsingleton truth-value classification without witness transport, and the universal raw-pair form without explicit witness or certification data remains unproved.
boundary: With per-side realization together with a cross-instance mathematical witness, or admissibility data with a pairwise bridge and canonical transport equalities, universal quasi-functors with target packages exist between admissible instances on the original carriers. With realization alone, or with constant target-returning maps, comparison collapses to subsingleton biconditionals built from stored inhabitants, classifying by truth values while failing to transport stage witnesses. The missing witness, blueprint and coherence data mark the divide, located by the equivalence between admission and the three Nonempty components and by the result that an inhabited certified catalog still requires universal certification and blueprints.

conclusions.statement: For any raw instances L1 and L2, given an unrestricted mathematical witness W, the type of universal quasi-functors between the internally built source and target admissible instances is nonempty.
For any raw instances L1 and L2, given that an unrestricted witness exists, there exist admissible instances A1 and A2 on L1 and L2 with a universal quasi-functor between them.
For any admissible instances A1 and A2, given a comparison witness W, the type of universal quasi-functors between A1 and A2 is nonempty.
For any admissible instances A1 and A2, given a mathematical support witness W, the type of universal quasi-functors between A1 and A2 is nonempty.

For any raw instances L1 and L2, given source realization existence, target realization existence and support witness existence, there exist admissible instances A1 and A2 on L1 and L2 with a universal quasi-functor between them.
For any raw instances L1 and L2, given admissibility data for L1 and L2 and a transport bridge between them, there exist admissible instances on L1 and L2 with a universal quasi-functor between them.
For all raw instances L1 and L2, admitting an unrestricted witness holds if and only if source realization exists, target realization exists and a mathematical support witness exists.
For all raw instances L1 and L2, the witness-free residual obligation holds if and only if the pair admits an unrestricted witness.
There exist admissible instances A1 and A2 on the Godel 1931 and DP-emitter carriers with a universal quasi-functor between them.
There exist admissible instances A1 and A2 on the benchmark-transport and DP-emitter carriers with a universal quasi-functor via the strong transport bridge.
For any clause structure L and sentence phi, given that phi is boundary and reimport, False follows.
There exists an annotated structure with overlapping boundary and reimport such that no original clause structure with the same boundary and reimport data exists.
Given an inhabited certified boundary catalog, universal certification and universal certified-pair blueprints both hold.
For any instances L1 and L2, the quasi-functor type is a subsingleton and the comparison-witness type is a subsingleton.
The coarse annotation class does not factor through typed conclusion, witnessed by two licensed states with the same class and distinct conclusions.

openPoints: Universal certification for every raw instance is carried as an explicit hypothesis for universal residual and witness-free results.
Universal certified-pair blueprints are carried as an explicit hypothesis and are not built from the overlay alone.

Unrestricted, classification and bridge theorems require an explicit witness, admissibility data with pairwise bridge data, and four canonical coherence equalities; the bare universal form over all raw pairs with no hypotheses is not proved.
The weak bridge route yields constant target-returning transports; source-sensitive transport needs the strong transport-bridge route with caller-supplied transports.
Admissibility alone yields a carrier assembled from target-local data without source-to-target transport and asserts no parallelism without comparison data.
The coarse DP annotation observer collides on distinct licensed conclusions, and actual DP semantics admits no extensional factorization through the wrapper coordinate.

subTopics.name: Schema, typed theories and license carriers
Clause repair, canonical fixtures and DP instances
Unrestricted identity, witness-free closure and P4C residual

files.summary: Packages four ablation facts about the KO7 orientation barrier. Shows removing duplication admits a simple size rank while simple typing preserves additive and affine barriers. Shows a sharing-aware counter decreases on the displayed step, contrasting with the tree obstruction.
files.conclusion: The four ablation facts jointly compare duplication, typing and sharing as factors in the KO7 barrier.

files.summary: This file defines an explicit hypothesis package pairing a runtime engine contract with source and target LCEL instances and a residual package, plus a consequence record with unrestricted-witness admission and witness-free structural identity. It proves the advertised typed-refusal surface remains in refusal support under that package. It proves the LCEL admission and universal-license conclusions follow once the residual obligation is supplied, which the contract does not synthesize alone.
files.conclusion: Paired with an explicit residual package, the engine contract yields LCEL unrestricted admission and structural identity without synthesizing the residual itself.

files.summary: Defines sound closed-carrier adapters for the root Step relation where source termination is derived from a well-founded target and orientation proof. Inhabits polynomial-interpretation and multiset-path-order adapters. Proves a total seven-family ledger with two supported and five NO-TRANSPORT families with named missing structure.
files.conclusion: Exactly two of seven adapter families are supported with certified transport and five remain NO-TRANSPORT with named missing structure.

files.summary: Defines record-emission interfaces for a base-duplicating system, including witnesses, faithful emitters, semantic and rank-level projection kernels, and conservation emitters. Proves live coordinates are constant and non-injective while record coordinates are injective and retrieving, yielding sequential uncertainty reduction at stage one and a hidden-state requirement. Realizes all interfaces on free-term syntax with wrapper erasure and counter-depth rank, yielding computation-to-confession bridges and an OperationalIncompleteness package.
files.conclusion: Every faithful and projective record emitter with 1 ≤ K realizes the computation-to-record crossing and, with projection rank, the computation-to-confession bridge, instantiated on free syntax.

files.summary: This file packages schema realization with four proof-carrying support records as admissibility data. It defines lifting to admissible instances and supplies canonical packages for the Godel 1931, benchmark-transport and DP-emitter instances. It proves each lifted package is definitionally equal to its separately declared admissible instance.
files.conclusion: The three canonical LCEL packages lift definitionally to their separately declared admissible instances.

files.summary: Defines proof-carrying annotated derivations that keep base versus licensed provenance, with partial erasure returning none on licensed proofs. Defines license relabeling, licensed-payload projection and total payload sum with an equivalence and round trips. Proves every extension derivation reimports with a license, and that at a boundary sentence with no base derivation no annotated derivation erases to base.
files.conclusion: Every extension derivation reimports as a licensed annotated derivation, but no annotated derivation of a boundary sentence erases to a base derivation.

files.summary: Builds a support-comparison witness between the benchmark-transport and native DP emitter LCEL instances by composing through the Godel side. Derives the admissible comparison witness and the universal quasi-functor package with inhabitation. The header states this gives proposition-level equivalences from inhabitants, not evidence-preserving direct DP transport.
files.conclusion: Benchmark-transport and native DP emitter admissible instances are propositionally equivalent via a Godel-composed comparison witness.

files.summary: Defines an explicit bijection between two two-constructor sentence types sending base to baseSystem and blocked witness to licensedProjection with nonconstancy. Populates boundary, annotation, base-sentence and proposition-valued license and reimport correspondences with strong preservation laws. Builds route semantics, bridge data, support and unrestricted witnesses yielding quasi-functor inhabitation and admissibility through several routes.
files.conclusion: An explicit nonconstant finite correspondence yields inhabited quasi-functors and unrestricted witnesses between benchmark-transport and DP emitter instances via multiple routes.

files.summary: Formalizes LCEL clauses on boundary underivability, licensed extension derivability and reimport conservativity over an abstract sentence type. Proves the three clauses force boundary and reimport disjoint. Exhibits a two-sentence Godel-shaped model where the boundary lies in the reimport class, refuting conservativity, then introduces annotated clauses replacing conservativity by licensed annotated return and shows the same configuration inhabits the strictly weaker repair.
files.conclusion: Original boundary plus conservativity clauses forbid boundary-reimport overlap, while the annotated repair admits the Godel-shaped overlap and is strictly weaker.

files.summary: Places Godel-shaped and typed DP fixtures as inhabited annotated-clause records with exact base, extension and annotated derivability characterizations. Gives concrete boundary extension and annotated proofs with payload receipt and erasure none. Proves the unlicensed control underivable on all three layers and that the DP boundary-reimport overlap cannot inhabit old plain-base conservativity.
files.conclusion: Both Godel-shaped and concrete DP fixtures inhabit annotated clauses with exact derivability, and the DP overlap refutes plain-base conservativity.

files.summary: Shows any two realized LCEL slot profiles are stagewise equivalent and any two realized instances compare via six iff fields ignoring inputs. Exhibits a contentless all-True profile equivalent to every realized profile. Proves both quasi-functor and comparison-witness hom-sets are subsingletons, so the six-slot comparison is a classification and the cited structural identity is conditional transport, not carrier identity.
files.conclusion: Six-slot LCEL comparison is a subsingleton classification, not a transport of witnesses.

files.summary: Combines a projection-certification theorem for the free duplicator with a finite two-tag LCEL fixture using constant True predicates and identity maps. Defines base, obstruction, reflection and reimport contents with coherence and a comparison object. Assembles the LCEL instance and projects schema realization with base, license-transfer, reimport-transfer and factorization supports, without external interpretation.
files.conclusion: The finite DP emitter fixture realizes the LCEL schema and supplies base, license-transfer, reimport-transfer and factorization supports.

files.summary: Defines boundary as failure to factor through an observer, equivalent to non-fiber-constancy, and proves a nontrivial kernel forbids any left inverse so split projections can be irreversible. Develops reversible and irreversible coordinate models where sensitivity implies boundary admissibility with set equality under extensional completeness. Realizes the interfaces on a Boolean fixture and on KO7 traces with dpRank versus wrapper multiplicity, including no-transport obstructions.
files.conclusion: Boundary sensitivity to the irreversible coordinate is underivable in the base layer, concretely witnessed by wrapper parity versus dpRank.

files.summary: Defines source-sensitive route semantics from caller-supplied slot correspondence, stagewise equivalence, target admission and coherence equalities. Defines base, license, reimport and boundary transports from those fields. Builds transport-bridge and mathematical support witnesses from admissibility data plus canonical equalities, with lemmas that witness transports project to route transports.
files.conclusion: Caller-supplied correspondences and equalities build coherent transport-bridge and support witnesses with transports projecting to the route maps.

files.summary: Constructs universal quasi-functors operationally from mathematical support witnesses using slot correspondence and transport of source base, license, reimport and boundary theorems. States transport-coherence regressions and transported sentence identities as named lemmas. Derives inhabitation directly and via support downgrade, with Godel to DP and Godel to benchmark corollaries.
files.conclusion: Mathematical support witnesses yield inhabited universal quasi-functors, instantiated for Godel-DP and Godel-benchmark pairs.

files.summary: This file defines the LCELMathematicalSupportWitness record that bundles a strong semantic slot correspondence, source and target base, license, reimport and boundary theorems, coherence equalities, and transport maps. It provides projections to correspondences and single theorems, together with equalities showing each transported source theorem equals the stored target theorem. It defines transports of base, license, reimport and boundary theorems through a strong slot correspondence and builds concrete witnesses for the Gödel to benchmark and Gödel to DP-emitter pairs.
files.conclusion: Source base, license, reimport and boundary theorems transport to target instances along a strong semantic slot correspondence, instantiated for Gödel to benchmark and Gödel to DP pairs.

files.summary: This file packages conditional route, admissibility, coherence and boundary data for LCEL pairs and isolates the universal residual that remains an explicit caller obligation. It defines certified instance overlays, certified-pair blueprints with four canonical coherence equations, residual packages, and a certified boundary catalog. It proves conditional reductions showing universal certification plus blueprints yield residual packages, unrestricted witnesses and witness-free structural identity. It also builds the canonical benchmark to DP residual package and its corollaries without claiming raw unconditional P4C.
files.conclusion: Universal certification plus universal certified-pair blueprints yield a residual package and witness-free structural identity for every raw pair, while raw unconditional P4C remains unproved without that universal data.

files.summary: This file defines witness-parameterized proposition slots for base reversibility, license irreversibility and reimport reversibility, plus asymmetry and boundary factorization records for Paper C Propositions 5.8 and 5.9. It defines stronger proof-carrying base, license, reimport and factorization support records with adapters building them from semantic theorems. It populates canonical Gödel-side and benchmark-side support and witness packages from the available semantic-support fields.
files.conclusion: Stronger proof-carrying base, license, reimport and factorization supports assemble into reversibility-asymmetry and boundary-factorization packages, instantiated for Gödel and benchmark instances.

files.summary: This file closes Paper C Propositions 5.8 and 5.9 and the artifact-facing structural-identity theorem unconditionally on the typed FormalLCELInstance carrier. It shows every typed instance carries base, license and reimport semantic supports and builds universal proof-carrying support records. It proves any two instances are stagewise equivalent through the DP pivot with universally inhabited license and reimport equivalences, yielding quasi-functors in both directions.
files.conclusion: Every pair of typed LCEL instances admits a quasi-functor in both directions, with reversibility asymmetry and boundary factorization holding unconditionally.

files.summary: This file extends the route-semantics layer into a lift surface for LCEL pairs. Given pair-generic source-sensitive route semantics, per-side admissibility data and four canonical coherence equations, the route lifts to a strong transport bridge, a mathematical-support witness and an unrestricted witness. It derives unrestricted-witness admission and unrestricted and existence-form structural identity corollaries while remaining conditional and not claiming raw-pair P4C.
files.conclusion: Route semantics with admissibility and coherence lifts to a transport bridge and unrestricted witness yielding structural identity, conditionally.

files.summary: This file represents Paper C Definition 5.7 as a packaged six-slot LCEL structure with its four structural clauses. It defines a light propositional profile with stagewise equivalence, typed boundary and annotation objects with realization lemmas, and a typed FormalLCELInstance adjoining explicit license and reimport slots. It builds canonical Gödel-labelled and benchmark transport instances and proves each realizes the schema.
files.conclusion: The six-slot LCEL schema is packaged as a typed instance carrier with canonical Gödel and benchmark instances each realizing the schema.

files.summary: The file defines weak maps between LCEL instances for boundary witnesses, external-license propositions, reimport-class propositions and annotations, bundled as LCELSemanticSlotCorrespondence. It defines strengthened records adding one-way preservation implications plus a one-way base-sentence map, bundled as LCELStrongSemanticSlotCorrespondence with a downgrade to the weak bundle. It constructs canonical Godel-to-benchmark and Godel-to-DP maps that are constant to target-designated values, proving the stated equalities and implications from target support fields.
files.conclusion: Constant Godel-to-DP and Godel-to-benchmark maps satisfy the weak and strong slot equations using only target support fields.

files.summary: The file defines LCELQuasiFunctor as six proposition-level biconditionals between LCEL slot profiles with clause access, symmetry, composition and transport of realization. It defines comparison, semantic and support witnesses packaging stagewise profile equivalence with license, reimport and support equivalences and rebuilding reversibility and factorization packages. It instantiates these witnesses for Godel-to-benchmark and Godel-to-DP pairs and proves stagewise equivalence with bidirectional realization transport and structural identity.
files.conclusion: Godel, benchmark-transport and DP-emitter LCEL instances are pairwise stagewise equivalent with bidirectional realization transport and structural identity.

files.summary: The file defines four proof-carrying records for base provable-unprovable pairs, blocked-sentence reflection, reimport certification and boundary factorization, with projections to proposition-only witness interfaces. It provides extraction functions packaging fields from base, license, reimport and boundary support records. It instantiates all four packages for Godel, benchmark-transport and DP-emitter instances.
files.conclusion: For each of the Godel, benchmark and DP instances the file yields packaged provable-unprovable, reflection, certification and factorization records projected from support records.

files.summary: The file builds a typed two-sentence DP theory where the base layer derives only transformed-call termination while source termination is empty, and the extension adds a licensed source proof retaining certificate and KO7 license. It defines the active certificate-consuming license routing the pair certificate through a natural countdown and polynomial rank, keeping the constant map only as a fixture. It proves source termination is reference-true yet underivable, gives an exact alphabet proxy that fails truth preservation, and proves the coarse annotation observer collides with distinct conclusions so no extensional factorization exists.
files.conclusion: The coarse annotation class fails to determine typed conclusion on actual licensed DP reimports, and actual DP semantics admits no extensional factorization.

files.summary: The file defines TypedTheory as a sentence type with a derivation family, DerivationMorphism mapping sentences and derivations, and TheoryExtension adding sentence and fiberwise derivation injectivity. It defines identity and composition for both morphisms and extensions with pointwise action laws and associativity. It provides the forgetful passage from extensions to morphisms.
files.conclusion: Identity and composition give associative sentence- and derivation-level maps with genuine extensions composing and forgetting to morphisms.

files.summary: The file defines typed external-license objects with framework, licensed sentence and designated reflection and truth fields, and typed reimport-class objects with admission, imported sentence and certification fields. It defines propositional realizations with designated witnesses realizing them. It constructs default objects from any formal external classical comparison and proves their realizations equivalent to hasReflectionOperator and hasSemanticReimport.
files.conclusion: Default license and reimport objects from any external classical comparison realize exactly when the underlying reflection and reimport existentials hold.

files.summary: This file defines admissible LCEL instances bundling a typed instance with schema realization and four substrate support records, and universal quasi-functors carrying a slot-level quasi-functor plus target reversibility and boundary packages. It constructs a universal quasi-functor by genuine source-to-target transport through an admissibility comparison witness, and proves the universal structural-identity theorem and its bidirectional form from such a witness. It also defines a weaker admissibility-only packaging that builds the carrier from target data without transport, and instantiates all constructions on the Godel, benchmark-transport and DP emitter pairs.
files.conclusion: For any admissible pair equipped with a comparison witness, a universal quasi-functor with genuinely transported target packages exists, instantiated on the Godel-DP and Godel-benchmark pairs.

files.summary: This file characterizes when a raw pair of LCEL instances admits an unrestricted mathematical witness as the conjunction of schema realization on each side and a cross-instance mathematical support witness. It packages this as classification data and proves the biconditional and its bridge-data refinements using per-side admissibility data plus pairwise slot correspondence and stagewise equivalence. It builds support witnesses by two routes, a weak route with constant target-returning transports and a strong route storing caller-supplied transports with canonical coherence, and instantiates both on the Godel-DP and Godel-benchmark pairs.
files.conclusion: Admission of an unrestricted witness is equivalent to per-side admissibility plus pairwise bridge data, realized on the canonical Godel pairs.

files.summary: This file defines the propositional predicate AdmitsLCELUnrestrictedWitness hiding the choice of unrestricted witness. It proves the existence-form universal theorem producing admissible instances with the original carriers and a universal quasi-functor from mere existence of a witness. It discharges witness existence and the existence-form conclusion on the Godel-DP and Godel-benchmark pairs via canonical witnesses.
files.conclusion: Mere existence of an unrestricted witness yields admissible instances on the original carriers with a universal quasi-functor, instantiated on the two canonical pairs.

files.summary: This file defines unrestricted mathematical witnesses over raw instance pairs packaging per-side realization and a full mathematical support witness. It builds source and target admissible instances internally from the witness and lifts the closed Track G theorem to prove the unrestricted universal structural-identity theorem with Track G transport, plus bidirectional and canonical Godel-pair corollaries. Four hardening lemmas record that the construction coincides definitionally with the Track G and Route E1 pipelines.
files.conclusion: Any raw pair equipped with an unrestricted mathematical witness yields a universal quasi-functor between internally built admissible instances via Track G transport.

files.summary: This file proves classification-scoped witness-free structural-identity theorems that replace the witness argument by Nonempty hypotheses, per-side admissibility data plus bridges, or concrete classification packages. It gives weak bridge and strong transport-bridge refinements constructing the witness internally with constant versus bridge-supplied transports. It closes Godel-DP, Godel-benchmark and benchmark-DP corollaries through both routes while stating the hypothesis-free universal form is not proved.
files.conclusion: On the classified scope, per-side and bridge hypotheses suffice for admissible instances with a universal quasi-functor, closed on the three canonical pairs.

files.summary: This file builds a concrete TRS engine contract and its LCEL P4C residual-hypothesis package. The package uses the typed-output classifier, benchmark-transport source, DP-emitter target, and route-lift residual. It checks refusal-surface support and that the admitted residual witnesses equal the benchmark DP witnesses.
files.conclusion: The TRS contract classifier stays in refusal support and admits the LCEL P4C residual with benchmark DP witnesses.

files.summary: This file pins the LCEL comparison degeneracy without proving new theorems. It checks stagewise LCEL from realization, the contentless profile with realization and stagewise lemmas, quasi-functors from realization, contentless comparison, subsingletons for quasi-functors and comparisons, and identity as classification. It also prints axioms.
files.conclusion: Contentless LCEL realization yields subsingleton comparisons with identity as classification.

files.summary: This file exercises DP-emitter LCEL instance declarations and their axiom footprints. It checks formal-external comparison support at semantic and transfer levels, schema realization, semantic base and license or reimport transfer supports, reversibility asymmetry and boundary factorization, license and reimport content equations, Godel-DP comparison witnesses, and bidirectional structural identity.
files.conclusion: The DP-emitter LCEL instance realizes the schema with supported comparisons, asymmetry, factorization, and Godel-DP structural identity.

files.summary: This file pairs check with print-axioms for LCEL reversibility and boundary-factorization supports. It covers base, license-irreversibility, reimport, and boundary-factorization support types and their construction from semantic supports, stronger-support lemmas for asymmetry and factorization, and Godel 1931, benchmark-transport, and DP-emitter instances.
files.conclusion: The file records reachability and axiom footprints for LCEL reversibility supports across Godel, benchmark, and DP-emitter instances.

files.summary: This file exercises the unconditional LCEL closure theorems on canonical instances. It checks universal semantic, base, license, reimport, and factorization supports, unconditional reversibility asymmetry and boundary factorization, universal stagewise equivalence and witness equivalences, and unconditional uni- and bidirectional structural-identity quasi-functors for Godel and DP-emitter instances.
files.conclusion: Unconditional reversibility asymmetry, factorization, stagewise equivalence, and bidirectional structural identity hold for the Godel and DP-emitter LCEL instances.

files.summary: This file exercises typed Sigma-Gamma license and reimport objects for Godel, benchmark-transport, and DP-emitter instances. It checks object existence, realized propositions, realized-witness equivalences, designated-sentence equalities, reflection, admission, certification and truth lemmas, and cross-instance blocked and imported sentence equations.
files.conclusion: License and reimport objects are realized with matching witnesses and designated-sentence properties across all three LCEL instances.

claims.reason: The FormalLCELInstance structure defines the LCEL schema object named by the entry.

claims.paper: Observer Determinacy of Termination Certificates: Sufficient Statistics, Blackwell Comparison, and Simple Projections for Step-Duplicating Recursion
claims.heading: Prop. 15.10
claims.reason: The two definitions embed base derivations and reimport extension derivations with explicit licenses, and the two theorems give existence of reimported proof objects with payload round-trip reversibility. No single declaration states embedding, reimport and reversibility together.

claims.paper: Observer Determinacy of Termination Certificates: Sufficient Statistics, Blackwell Comparison, and Simple Projections for Step-Duplicating Recursion
claims.heading: Prop. 15.11
claims.reason: The underivability, admissibility and set-equality theorems give the three factorization claims under the stated base-factorization and completeness structures. No single declaration states all three.

claims.paper: Observer Determinacy of Termination Certificates: Sufficient Statistics, Blackwell Comparison, and Simple Projections for Step-Duplicating Recursion
claims.heading: Thm. 15.12
claims.reason: The identity, bidirectional, transport and subsingleton theorems together give two-way transport, existence under shape and witness hypotheses, and subsingleton comparison types for the six-slot record. No single declaration states the whole record claim.

claims.paper: Observer Determinacy of Termination Certificates: Sufficient Statistics, Blackwell Comparison, and Simple Projections for Step-Duplicating Recursion
claims.heading: Prop. 15.14
claims.reason: The two Boundary theorems give same counter rank with different parity and multiplicity, and the factorization definition with sensitivity, admissibility and underivability theorems give non-derivability through counter rank. No single declaration states independence and underivability together.

claims.paper: Observer Determinacy of Termination Certificates: Sufficient Statistics, Blackwell Comparison, and Simple Projections for Step-Duplicating Recursion
claims.heading: Rem. 15.25
claims.reason: The subterm-criterion and free-recursor theorems give termination, while the collapse, factoring, descent-deposit and preservation theorems give multiplicity collapse along counter descent. No single declaration states collapse and termination together.
